acme-cs: Hey team — customer sent this repro: rerank API returns 422 when their payload nests 'query' inside documents, and when it doesn't error the scores are all 0. Ticket #C-8247. Payload snippet below.
acme-cs: ```json
{
  \"documents\": [
    {\"id\": \"d1\", \"query\": \"user intent\", \"candidates\": [{\"id\": \"c1\", \"text\": \"candidate text\"}]}
  ],
  \"query\": \"search phrase\"
}
```
acme-cs: They say they followed the docs but tried nesting because their search indexing pipeline produces docs with internal candidate arrays.

tara: thanks — tagging eng. quick Q: which endpoint version are they hitting? v1/rerank or v1/rerank-alpha?

acme-cs: v1/rerank, using api.redwood.com, content-type application/json, auth via API key.

mike: reading this — our rerank expects either top-level \"candidates\" (array of candidate objects) OR a top-level \"documents\" array with each document having a flat text field or passages. We don't support candidates nested inside documents in that v1 shape. nesting likely caused our schema validation to miss candidates -> 422. Also having \"query\" both at top-level and inside a doc could confuse our server-side mapping.

jessica: got it. common pitfalls:
- \"query\" should be a single string at the root (or use \"query_key\" only for vector search bindings) — avoid per-document \"query\" name.
- If you want per-document passages, use: \"documents\": [{\"id\":\"d1\",\"passages\":[{\"id\":\"p1\",\"text\":\"...\"}]}], and the service will flatten passages as candidates internally.
- We currently validate that when \"documents\" contains a \"candidates\" field we return 422 because that shape conflicts with the primary candidates input.

mike: repro steps for eng to reproduce:
1) POST /v1/rerank with payload exactly as the customer sent (include nested candidates)
2) observe 422 validation error with body: {\"error\":\"invalid_input\",\"message\":\"nested candidates inside documents not supported\"}
3) remove nested candidates and instead flatten to top-level candidates or convert to passages -> then scores are produced but if they keep an inner \"query\" field sometimes our scoring lambda reads the inner field and returns zeros because it treats query as empty (bug: precedence of per-doc query was wrong)

acme-cs: we reproduced locally, 422 when nested. But even with flattened candidates, scores are 0 when their doc objects have an empty \"text\" field logically (they were using \"content\" instead of \"text\"). so two issues collided.

tara: thanks — important to call out mapping mismatches: the schema requires candidate objects to include a \"text\" (or \"content\" mapping via our adapter only in some SDKs). If the customer sends {\"content\":...} in raw JSON the server doesn't remap and returns 0 scores because model receives empty prompt.

jessica: quick mitigation to share with customer:
- Flatten their pipeline to emit top-level \"candidates\": [{\"id\":\"c1\",\"text\":\"...\"}, ...]
- Ensure root-level \"query\": \"search phrase\" and remove per-document \"query\" keys.
- Or use documents->passages shape: {\n  \"documents\": [{\"id\":\"d1\",\"passages\": [{\"id\":\"p1\",\"text\":\"...\"}]}],\n  \"query\":\"search phrase\"\n}

mike: I'll open an internal issue for validation error message clarity — 422 should say \"remove nested candidates; use top-level candidates or documents->passages\". Also adding a linter in the SDKs to detect common field aliases like \"content\" vs \"text\".

support-bot: Ticket C-8247 updated: escalated to eng. Assigned to mike. ETA next business day.

acme-cs: customer accepted flatten workaround, but asked if backend can accept nested candidate arrays so they don't rewrite indexing. asked for timeline.

mike: short term — provide mapping guidance + example script to convert index output to top-level candidates. long term — evaluating accepting nested candidates in a future minor version but needs careful schema disambiguation and perf tests.

tara: i'll send the conversion snippet to the customer now and document the caveat in our rerank docs (query_name collisions + accepted shapes). also cc: docs-team for clear example.

acme-cs: thanks, please include exact sample curl and python SDK example.

jessica: sample curl to flatten:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"query\":\"search phrase\",\"candidates\":[{\"id\":\"c1\",\"text\":\"candidate text\"}]}'
```

mike: note for eng: also add an explicit 422 message for nested candidates and a doc link.

tara: marked resolved with workaround; keeping thread open until docs PR merged. :white_check_mark:
